fine_trace.code: if (!parse_host (p, hostend - p, flags, host, error))
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled URI string reaches parse_host with the host component starting at p; for an IPv6 literal the host begins with '['.
The IPv6 literal contents (between brackets) are copied into a heap buffer of length-1 bytes; the '%' scope marker is located inside this buffer.
pct points to the '%' character in the heap-allocated addr buffer; its position is attacker-controlled by placing '%' near the end of the IPv6 literal.

Without a bounds check, pct[1], pct[2], and pct[3] are read from addr. When pct is near the end of the buffer, these reads access memory past the heap allocation, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ.
